newsitem.title: USA: ARCO plans $3.4 billion cap spending plan.
newsitem.headline: ARCO plans $3.4 billion cap spending plan.

text.p: Atlantic Richfield Co Wednesday said its board of directors approved a $3.4 billion capital spending plan for 1997, up from $3.3 billion in 1996.
In a statement, ARCO also said it replaced 133 percent of its consolidated worldwide oil and gas production last year.

"Strong performance in terms of 1996 reserve additions and increased capital spending are indicative of the opportunities we have to grow ARCO's upstream businesses," said Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Mike Bowlin. "We will aggressively pursue these opportunities, both overseas and in the U.S."
ARCO said it added 468 million barrels of oil equivalent (BOE) to proved reserves in 1996 while producing 353 million BOE.
The largest source of increased overseas production came from Rhourde El Baguel field in Algeria where ARCO has a partnership with the national oil company, SONATRACH.
With enhanced oil recovery techniques, ARCO expects to nearly double recovery from that field, which booked 218 million barrels of oil equivalent (BOE) reserves for 1996.
Bowlin said ARCO's upstream oil and gas business is expected to account for over 60 percent of 1997 spending, or $2.1 billion, up from $1.7 billion in 1996.
ARCO's overseas projects will account for more than half of the upstream budget, or $1.2 billion, Bowlin said, compared with $820 million in 1996.

"The 1997 plan includes a full year's work in developing enhanced oil recovery at Rhourde El Baguel, and we plan to move our Indonesian gas discovery, Wiriagar, further toward commercialization," Bowlin said.
The company may also put more money into projects with LUKARCO, its joint venture with Russia's largest oil company, LUKOIL.
ARCO plans to spend $235 million in Alaska this year for development of the new Alpine field, declared commercial in October 1996.
The field comprised 65 million of the 94 million BOE added to reserves last year, ARCO said.
The Alpine field is expected to start production in 2000. Added reserves also came from Prudhoe Bay, Kuparuk and Niakuk fields, which totalled around 29 million barrels of oil .
